description: Perform one manufacturing step using preview=true first, then repeat the identical request with sourceVersion from the preview, previewReceipt and a fresh idempotencyKey after review. Read get_manufacturing_order first: its productionMode says which steps the order takes. Actions: create_draft (warehouseId and 1–50 lines; optional plannedStartAt and plannedCompletionAt as YYYY-MM-DD dates), issue (manufacturingOrderId). quick_build orders (an account with Quick Build but not full Manufacturing, as the screen's Build and Build All): build_line (MO + lineId; completedQuantity builds part of what is left, omitted all of it) and build_all (MO; everything left on every line, all or nothing) consume the components from the order's warehouse and receive the finished goods there in one step, with no work orders or pick lists; issuing such an order does not check stock, the build does. work_orders orders (full Manufacturing): start_pick/collect/complete_pick (MO + pickListId; collect also needs pickListItemId and actual collection), start_work/complete_work (MO + workOrderId). issue refuses an order with material shortages unless issueDespiteShortages=true, which the user must decide, as the screen's Issue Anyway. start_work needs the work order's picking complete. complete_work requires the actual completed quantity: the full planned output, or on an account with work order QA, the units QA accepted after record_work_order_qa finished the inspection; use the work-order UI for other partial output. Lot- or expiry-tracked output needs trackingLot / trackingExpiry (build_all: lineTracking per line); serials are generated. Each step uses canonical production/picking services. Requires Write + manufacturing.execute on an unpinned operator credential. In-app assistants get a confirm card the user applies.

completedQuantity.description: complete_work: the actual output quantity. build_line: the units to build, at most what is left on the line; omit to build all that is left.

issueDespiteShortages.description: issue: true to issue even though materials are short, as the screen's Issue Anyway does; only when the user decides to. The preview lists the shortages. Not used on a Quick Build account, where issuing does not check stock.

lineId.description: build_line: the manufacturing order line to build.

lineTracking.description: build_all: the finished goods' lot and/or expiry for each line whose item tracks them.

trackingExpiry.description: The finished goods' expiry, YYYY-MM-DD; required when the line's item is expiry-tracked.

trackingLot.description: The finished goods' lot; required when the line's item is lot-tracked.

note.description: build_line and build_all: an optional note kept on the build.

plannedCompletionAt.description: create_draft: the planned completion day, YYYY-MM-DD.

plannedStartAt.description: create_draft: the planned start day, YYYY-MM-DD.

trackingExpiry.description: build_line and complete_work: the finished goods' expiry, YYYY-MM-DD; required when the output item is expiry-tracked.

trackingLot.description: build_line and complete_work: the finished goods' lot; required when the output item is lot-tracked.
